        c=o.get('message',{}).get('content',[])
        t=' '.join(b.get('text','') for b in c if isinstance(b,dict) and b.get('type')=='text').strip()
        if len(t.split())>=25: rows.append((i,t))
def strip(t):
    t=re.sub(r'```.*?```','',t,flags=re.S);t=re.sub(r'`[^`]*`','',t);t=re.sub(r'\|.*\|','',t);return t
def stats(rs):
    if not rs: return None
    W=[];S=[];T=0;E=0;B=0
    for _,t in rs:
        t=strip(t);w=t.split();W.append(len(w))
        ss=[x for x in re.split(r'(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+',t) if len(x.split())>2]

        E+=t.count('—');B+=len(re.findall(r'\*\*',t))//2
        T+=len(re.findall(r'(?i)\b(leverage|utilize|robust|seamless|delve|crucial|comprehensive|streamline)\b',t))
    n=len(rs)
    return dict(n=n,avg_words=round(sum(W)/n),avg_sent=round(sum(S)/len(S),1),over25=round(100*sum(x>25 for x in S)/len(S)),emdash=round(E/n,2),bold=round(B/n,1),tells=round(T/n,2))
pre=[r for r in rows if r[0]<cut];post=[r for r in rows if r[0]>cut]
print('cut line',cut);print('before',stats(pre));print('after',stats(post))
EOF

{ cat <<'EOF'
# Plain English style: rule-group ablation (feat-b368375d)

Model: sonnet, `claude -p --max-turns 1 --no-session-persistence`, style text via `--append-system-prompt`, one empty cwd per run, runs one at a time, stdin closed.
Design: 6 variants x 10 prompts x 3 reps = 180 runs. All 180 valid (no empty replies, no max-turns hits, no retries needed). 30 valid runs per variant.
Prompts: the 7 in eval/prompts.psv plus 3 status-style prompts (status1..3), see prompts.psv in this folder.
Metrics are on prose only: code fences, inline code, URLs and table rows removed. `words` = prose words. `pctLong` = % of sentences over 25 words. `tells` = lint.ts strict counts of vocab+filler+opener+negclose+emdash. `repeats` = number of distinct 6-word sequences that appear twice or more.

## Results (means over 30 runs)

EOF
bun $A/analyze.ts
cat <<'EOF'

## How to read the noise

Two spreads for `full`: T1 (SD of the three rep-means, each over 10 prompts) is very small, so it flags almost everything. T2 (SD of one prompt across its 3 reps, per-run) is the stricter bar. In the table, "REAL" = beats T1 and T2 is not tracked separately in the label except "weak" = beats T1 only. Read it this way:
- Real: exceeds T2 (per-run spread). Only `none` vs `full` clearly clears this: words -44 (T2 12.8), bold -1.7 (T2 1.0), avg sentence -2.4 (T2 2.2, borderline).
- `no-sentences` words +14.8 just clears T2 (12.8). Everything else is "weak" (beats T1 only) or within noise.
- With n=3 per cell, the weak flags are suggestive, not findings.

## Reading

1. The style as a whole works: 44 fewer words, shorter sentences, less bold than no style.
2. No single group accounts for it. Removing any one group leaves the reply near `full` (147-164 words against 149 full, 193 none). The groups overlap, so each can be cut or shrunk alone, but cutting several together is not tested.
3. Sentences is the only group whose removal moves something beyond per-run noise (words +15; repeated sequences +0.07, which is about 2 of 30 replies). Its effect on long sentences is within noise (+2.2 points).
4. Words, and Structure+Behavior: removal moves sentence length +1.0 and long-sentence share +3 to +3.6 points, weak at best. Nothing clears per-run noise.
5. AI tells: removal changes no tell count. The `none` variant already scores 0.00 tells, so these prompts and lint.ts cannot show any benefit. This is a floor effect. It is not evidence that the rules are useless on other prompts. `no-aitells` even had the lowest long-sentence share (0.0), within noise.
6. Behavior rules (act first, ask rarely) cannot be tested with `--max-turns 1` and tool-free prompts. They are untested, not shown useless.

## Token cost (chars / 4)

| Group | chars | ~tokens |
|---|---|---|
| preamble | 186 | 47 |
| Sentences | 338 | 85 |
| Words | 243 | 61 |
| Structure | 269 | 67 |
| AI tells | 987 | 247 |
| Behavior | 388 | 97 |
| What these rules do not change | 309 | 77 |
| Whole body | 2720 | ~680 |

## Recommendation

- Keep Sentences as is (85 tokens). Best measured effect.
- Shrink AI tells (247 tokens, 36% of the style) to the few items that cost little to state: the opener list, one em dash per paragraph, no closing summary. Aim ~80 tokens. Saves ~165 tokens. Evidence: no measurable effect here, but the base rate was already zero, so shrink rather than delete, and re-test with prompts that provoke tells (long explanations, advice).
- Shrink Words (61) to rules 1-2 (one word per meaning, same name for same thing). Aim ~30. Saves ~30 tokens. Weak evidence only.
- Structure (67): shrink to the bold-for-decisions and Warning lines. Aim ~35. Saves ~30. Weak evidence only.
- Keep Behavior (97) and "does not change" (77): not testable by this harness. Do not cut on this data.
- Total possible saving: about 225 tokens of 680 (~33%), mostly from AI tells.

## Limitations

- n=3 per cell (30 per variant, but only 3 per prompt). Differences smaller than T2 are noise.
- Preferences: runs started in empty directories outside the repo, so the repo's `outputStyle` setting (in .claude/settings.local.json) did not apply. ~/.claude/settings.json has no outputStyle and there is no ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. The `none` replies are visibly unstyled (long, numbered, bold-heavy), which confirms no style loaded. The mod, plugin hooks and saved memory were not checked beyond that.
- Sonnet, not necessarily the user's live model. A stronger model may follow the rules more tightly or need fewer of them.
- Single-turn, tool-free prompts. Real status turns after tool work are longer and may elicit more tells.
- Lint tells are near zero everywhere, so this metric cannot rank the AI tells group.
- Repeat detection (6-word sequences) is crude; it misses restating in other words.
EOF
} > $A/ablation-results.md; wc -l $A/ablation-results.md; grep -c REAL $A/ablation-results.md"}

cat > $B/prompts.psv <<'EOF'
launch|Write a launch announcement for Lintly, a new command-line tool that checks Markdown docs for broken links. It is aimed at developers.
product|Write a product description for a mechanical keyboard called the Anvil 75, with hot-swappable switches and an aluminum case.
readme|Write the opening paragraph of a README for an open-source library called Quill that parses log files quickly.
changelog|Write a changelog blurb for version 2.4 of our app: faster startup, a new dark theme, and a fix for a crash when importing CSV files.
status|Write a status update to my team: the database migration is 80 percent done, two tables remain, and we expect to finish Thursday.
cover|Write a short cover note for a job application for a backend engineer role at a mid-size fintech company. I have six years of Go experience.
plan|What do you think of my plan? I want to rewrite our whole backend in Rust over a weekend so it is faster. We have 40 services.
pitch|Write a one-paragraph pitch for a startup that sells a note-taking app for busy engineers.
linkedin|Write a LinkedIn post announcing that I just finished my first year as an engineering manager.
whymatters|Explain why code review matters for a software team.
EOF
cat > $B/build.ts <<'EOF'
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'fs'
const D = import.meta.dir
const src = readFileSync(D + '/style-origin.md', 'utf8')
const body = src.split(/^---$/m).slice(2).join('---').replace(/^\n/, '')
const parts = body.split(/^(?=## )/m)
const head = (p: string) => p.match(/^## (.*)/)?.[1] ?? ''
const sub = (name: string, text: string | null) => parts.map(p => head(p).startsWith(name) ? (text ?? '') : p).join('')
const slimAI = readFileSync(D + '/slim-aitells.txt', 'utf8')
const slimWords = readFileSync(D + '/slim-words.txt', 'utf8')
const slimStruct = readFileSync(D + '/slim-structure.txt', 'utf8')
mkdirSync(D + '/variants', { recursive: true })
const slimA = sub('AI tells', slimAI)
const v: Record<string, string> = {
  none: '', full: body, 'no-aitells': sub('AI tells', null), 'slim-aitells': slimA,
  'slim-all': (() => { let t = slimA; const ps = t.split(/^(?=## )/m); return ps.map(p => head(p).startsWith('Words') ? slimWords : head(p).startsWith('Structure') ? slimStruct : p).join('') })(),
}
for (const [k, t] of Object.entries(v)) writeFileSync(`${D}/variants/${k}.txt`, t)
for (const [k, t] of Object.entries(v)) console.log(k, t.length, '~' + Math.round(t.length / 4))
for (const f of ['slim-aitells', 'slim-words', 'slim-structure']) { const t = readFileSync(`${D}/${f}.txt`, 'utf8'); console.log(f, t.length, '~' + Math.round(t.length / 4)) }
EOF
cat > $B/slim-aitells.txt <<'EOF'
## AI tells (never write these)

1. Words: delve, pivotal, testament, tapestry, showcase, vibrant, crucial, seamless, holistic, robust, leverage, empower, transformative.
2. Phrases: "in order to", "it is important to note", "serves as", "not just X, but Y".
3. Openers: Great question, Absolutely, Certainly, Furthermore.
4. Hedges: "might possibly".
5. Form: one em dash per paragraph, no curly quotes, no trailing ", showcasing...".
6. Closers: no summary, no upbeat sign-off.

EOF
cat > $B/slim-words.txt <<'EOF'
## Words

1. One word for one meaning. Use simple verbs. No idioms or metaphors. Define abbreviations.

EOF
cat > $B/slim-structure.txt <<'EOF'
## Structure

1. Use a list or table for more than three items. Put decisions in **bold**. Warnings get their own line.
2. Lead with the outcome. Never restate the user's question.
3. Say each result once. Do not add a summary that repeats it.
4. Add one bolded "Decision for you" line only when the user must decide.
5. Never copy system-reminder or harness text into a reply.

EOF
bun $B/build.ts"}

new3 = "| `✔ go test`, `✘ go test (exit 1)`, `? npm test (exit unknown)` | Bash commands whose shape is a test (`go test`, `npm test`, `bun test`, `pytest`, `vitest`, `jest`, `claude plugin test`, `wipnote check`, …) or a build/check (`go build`, `go vet`, `tsc`, `claude plugin validate`, …). assert old5 in s; s = s.replace(old5, new5)

old6 = "- **Score**: `tells n · long n · em— n` is appended to the receipt line of every main-loop turn (strict rules). assert old6 in s; s = s.replace(old6, new6)
open(p,'w').write(s); print('README updated')

p='eval/README.md'; s=open(p).read()
old7 = "The six `long` hits that went away on the transcript were all list items with a bold label"

|---|---|---|---|---|
| long | 13 / 10 | 13 / 10 | 7 / 6 | 7 / 6 |
| opener | 0 | 0 | 3 / 3 | 3 / 3 |
| vocab | 0 | 0 | 2 / 2 (both meta) | 2 / 2 |
| punct | 0 | 0 | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |
| negclose | 0 | 0 | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |

other prose, not a fix for these replies. The one `negclose` hit is new transcript text ("The script is meant to
run one at a time. I did not check why."), five words after an affirmative sentence: it meets the narrowed rule.

The six `long` hits that went away on the transcript were all list items with a bold label"""
assert old7 in s; s = s.replace(old7, new7, 1)
open(p,'w').write(s); print('eval README updated')
EOF
)
